our_interpretation: Read as a retrospective claim that the seven GPT-4 predictions were substantively accurate. This does not require treating rhetorical descriptions as literal technical claims.

The assessment period starts in 2023, the year the original essay explicitly anticipated, and ends on 2025-07-27, when Marcus asserted vindication. Later developments cannot establish what had already happened by that assertion.

Persistent unreliability means material failures in relevant tasks, not an absence of improvement or usefulness. Successful integrations alone do not establish dependable interpretation of user intentions.

The seventh prediction includes longer-term claims about future architectures, a shift within a decade of December 2022, and historical judgments in 2043. These remain part of the referenced list; an unelapsed prediction is not a failed prediction.
A narrower reading referring only to the near-term warnings about errors and safety would receive substantially stronger support.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous evaluations substantiate the material predictions across the referenced list: persistent errors, unreliable reasoning and medical advice, hallucinations and guardrail weaknesses, unreliable downstream use, limited generality, unresolved alignment, and the claimed architectural trajectory. Supporting several warnings alone does not settle the whole list.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable evidence demonstrates that material predicted limitations did not persist or that a substantive prediction was false. A mixed finding requires both substantiated and refuted parts. Improvements, successful demonstrations, and unelapsed deadlines do not alone constitute refutation.

evidence.explanation: The study evaluates GPT-4 and GPT-3.5 and finds that misleading prompts can elicit biased outputs, supporting the guardrail and alignment warnings. It also reports substantial resistance to biased statements under benign prompts; the failures are not representative of every interaction.

evidence.locator: Abstract, following the GPT-4 diagnostic-performance result
evidence.explanation: Supports the original prediction that medical answers could contain consequential mistakes despite strong performance. This is a bounded clinical-assistant evaluation, not proof that every medical application is unreliable.

The GPT-4 update enabled structured function calls, including database and assistant uses, qualifying any blanket suggestion that integration was impractical. It does not establish dependable interpretation of intentions or error-free downstream behavior; the announcement also acknowledges unintended-action risks.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Clarification of which predictions the retrospective covers, plus dated evidence concerning outcomes through July 27, 2025 that establishes or refutes the remaining material assertions. Eventual outcomes of the longer-term forecasts would require separate assessment.
